markdown_report:
**Proposal: candidate-difficulty diagnostics for the existing single HSTU model.** At 0% progress, prioritize a controlled diagnostic extension before training changes.

**Starting insights.** First, training margins average 9.64–10.94 and negative-wins rates remain below 0.2%. This establishes fitted training-pair separation; validation ranking remains unmeasured.

Second, final-event deletion reduces margins by 3.10–4.06, while prefix shuffling changes them by approximately 0.01 or less. Endpoint sensitivity is evident, but deletion changes readout and coordinates.

Third, qualitative feedback separates relatedness, usefulness and evidence sufficiency. Histories establish neither ownership nor fulfilled needs; repeat and absent-prefix targets both remain training examples.

**Related-work insights.** Candidate construction changes metric values and model comparisons [1,2,6]. Uniform, frequency-matched and text-neighbor panels answer different questions; model-top-32 panels instead recover ranks through 32 and censor deeper ranks [7].

Activation-patching conclusions depend on corruption and scoring [3]. Identity controls and verified sites remain prerequisites; supplied internals differ from reference HSTU.

TREC distinguishes substitutes, complements and unknown compatibility [4]; evidence-sufficiency research motivates coverage reporting [5]. Repeat-consumption research additionally motivates shortcut-sensitive stratification [8,9], without treating repeats as errors.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Minimal next step | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking competition | Strong training margins | Paired candidate panels | Generalization |
| Sequence mechanisms | Endpoint sensitivity | Verified activation interventions | Causal interpretation |
| Recommendation evidence | Usefulness concerns | Span-supported rubric | Human calibration |
| Shortcut exposure | Repeat behavior can simplify ranking | Repeat/frequency/length strata | Memorization attribution |

**Atomic ideas and assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Originality: positive; negative | Potential: positive; negative | Difficulty: positive; negative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Candidate-panel audit [1,2,6] | 4/6/5 | Task-specific controls; established sampling | Clarifies competition; training-only evidence | Reuses scoring; eligibility and ties complicate implementation |
| Exact gate patching [3] | 5/6/7 | Mechanism-specific contrasts; established method | Localizes sensitivity; corruption dependence | No retraining; instrumentation required |
| Evidence-coverage audit [4,5] | 4/6/5 | Adapted rubric; established abstention | Separates unknowns; requires calibration | Public text; annotation burden |
| Repeat-stratified audit [8,9] | 3/6/3 | Focused integration; established distinction | Exposes shortcuts; cannot prove memorization | Causal prefixes; sparse strata |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain the candidate-panel audit, adding repeat stratification. Freeze one HSTU/category; inspect at most 128 eligible rows from ten batches. Fix final-position targets, seed 42, unique 32-item panels, exclusions and descending-score/item-ID tie ordering.

Pair uniform, frequency-matched, TF-IDF-neighbor and exact model-top panels on common text-eligible rows/universes; report exclusions, missingness, overlap and broader coverage. Record rank, maximum-alternative margin and outranking fraction by repeat status, training frequency and prefix length.

Interpret model-top rank as `min(r,33)` within its declared universe; hardness is selection-guaranteed. Restricted-universe results are not full-catalog results. Report ties and descriptive paired differences; unverified user identities preclude user-bootstrap intervals.

Preserve diagnostic interfaces and the measurement-grounded prompt. No inference/checkpoint changes occur. Keep all four routes and the pinned macro validation HR@10 selection unchanged; no uplift, dislike or compatibility claim follows.

idea.description: Extend DiagnosisProbe with reproducible, paired candidate panels for the existing single HSTU model, controlling candidate universe, row eligibility, tie ordering and repeated-target status. Distinguish sampled-panel competition from exact top-K rank censoring. Use one existing trained model per category, with no auxiliary recommendation model or inference fusion.
idea.motivation: Excellent separation against supplied training negatives leaves candidate difficulty and repeat-related shortcuts unresolved. The previous proposal understated implementation difficulty and overinterpreted model-mined panel competition: those alternatives are difficult by construction. A controlled audit can describe these distinctions without establishing held-out performance, current usefulness, compatibility, memorization or expected validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model and all ModelView hooks. Return metrics and metric_definitions alongside existing probes. Use the actual module's eval mode and torch.no_grad(), restoring its original mode in finally. Cache at most ten batches and select at most 128 base-eligible rows/category with a local seed-42 generator; preserve batch/row identifiers and never call them user IDs. Use final nonpadding positions determined by masked physical indices, never count-1. Require nonempty inputs, nonzero real-item positive targets and finite features/scores. Fix each row's original positive throughout the audit. For a shifted training target at position t, its causal input is sequence[:t+1]; repeat status, exclusions and history length must use that prefix, never subsequent positions. The primary final-position audit already has no subsequent nonpadding input. Truncate/right-align causal prefixes when needed and verify original causal-position scoring agrees with the reconstructed-prefix path before extending the audit to intermediate positions; physical-position embeddings can prevent agreement after repacking.

Derive item frequencies exclusively from public training histories. Use integer nearest-rank frequency quartile boundaries at ceil(q*N)-1 for q=.25,.5,.75 over real catalog items; assign bands with searchsorted(boundaries, count, side='left'). Equal frequencies stay together and empty bands are explicitly allowed. Publish boundaries, tie convention and catalog counts. Use the same quartiles for frequency matching and descriptive strata. Fix actual nonpadding length bins to 1–5, 6–10 and >=11; repeat status is target present/absent in the causal prefix, with optional occurrence count and distance from last occurrence. These measurements describe fitted training behavior even for absent-prefix targets.

Use only permitted titles/descriptions for local TF-IDF; do not access unavailable metadata fields or pretrained weights. Distinguish absent text, whitespace-only text, empty TF-IDF vectors and insufficient eligible positive-similarity neighbors. Freeze preprocessing as Unicode NFKC normalization, concatenated title and description, and TfidfVectorizer(lowercase=True, token_pattern=r'(?u)\b\w\w+\b', ngram_range=(1,2), min_df=1, max_features=50000, sublinear_tf=True, norm='l2', dtype=np.float32). Fit on permitted training-catalog metadata and persist vocabulary, IDF, catalog IDs and configuration beneath the trial directory. If fitting fails because the vocabulary is empty, mark text panels unavailable. Metadata availability at historical interaction times is unverified unless public release times establish it; report this limitation rather than altering benchmark splits or claiming temporal validity.

For the primary controlled comparison define each row's shared eligible alternative universe as real catalog items with nonzero TF-IDF vectors, excluding its target and visible causal-prefix item IDs. Require usable target text, >=32 alternatives overall, >=32 alternatives in the target frequency band, and >=32 alternatives with strictly positive target-text cosine. Select common-row eligibility before neural candidate scoring. Draw uniform and frequency-matched panels without replacement with independent stable streams constructed from seed 42, category index, cached batch index, row index and panel index, not Python's randomized hash. Rank text neighbors by descending cosine then ascending item ID. Retrieve exact model-top-32 alternatives through chunked scoring of the same shared universe using descending score then ascending item ID. Keep natural overlap; report pairwise intersection size/Jaccard and realized panel sizes. A target that appeared earlier is retained as the scored target while other seen items remain excluded; explicitly label this target-inclusive diagnostic convention.

Report the complete-case cohort separately from broader coverage: base-eligible counts, text eligibility, each panel's independent eligibility, common eligibility, and sequential plus nonexclusive exclusion reasons by category and stratum. Broader uniform/model-top analyses may use all real catalog alternatives, but must be separately labeled and cannot be pooled with the shared-text-universe comparison. Missing panels return null with reasons; never silently substitute candidates, zero scores or a smaller panel. Freeze row selection and non-model candidate IDs before comparing checkpoints. Exact model-top panels necessarily change with model scores; treat them as each model's own rank summary and record their IDs rather than claiming fixed-panel comparisons.

Apply a single total order everywhere: higher score ranks first, ties resolve by ascending item ID. An alternative outranks the target if its score is higher or its equal score has a smaller ID. Report score-tie counts/rates, positive rank, positive-minus-maximum-alternative margin and the fraction of alternatives ahead under this ordering. Raw margins are scale-dependent. For exact top-K retrieval over the declared universe, panel rank=min(r,K+1), where r is target rank over that universe plus target. At K=32, rank 33 means r>=33; panel HR@h equals that universe's HR@h for h<=32. Panel reciprocal rank and outranking fraction are censored summaries with floors/saturation, not full-universe MRR or win rate. Model-top maximum-alternative margin uses the actual strongest competitor; its hardness is guaranteed by mining and does not independently indicate miscalibration or poor discrimination. Restricted-text-universe identities do not imply full-catalog identities. Uniform sampling instead yields a hypergeometric ahead-count with expectation 32*(r-1)/N under the same total order and N eligible alternatives; sampled HR/MRR are protocol-specific.

Summarize paired differences between panels on identical complete-case rows, and descriptively stratify by frequency quartile, repeat status and length, including crossed strata and explicit counts; flag cells with fewer than 20 rows without treating this threshold as inferential validity. Loader identities are None, so provide neither user-level confidence intervals nor significance tests. If verified user identities later become available, aggregate repeated histories within users and bootstrap users within category using 1,000 seed-42 resamples. Candidate repeats, overlapping panels and training prefixes are dependent observations. Unobserved high-scoring alternatives remain possible relevant items, not confirmed negatives. Freeze diagnostic settings in advance to reduce adaptive diagnostic mining; only unchanged host four-category macro validation HR@10 selects training changes.

Retain all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, single-GPU execution and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Bound chunked scoring by the row cap and record actual computational cost. No retraining, inference changes or checkpoint changes are required. Each category continues to load exactly one independently trained HSTU checkpoint. A later architecture change must update checkpoint serialization, predictor writer and family-specific probes together. The interpretation prompt must embed measurements, definitions, counts, exclusions, missingness, universe scope, tie convention and training-only limitations without inventing uplift, ownership, satisfied needs or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
    was_training = self.view.model.training
    self.view.model.eval()
    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            cached = cache_at_most_ten_batches(train_loader)
            rows, base_counts = choose_base_eligible_rows(
                cached, max_rows=128, local_seed=42,
                final_index='max masked physical index',
                require_real_positive=True)
            frequency, boundaries = training_only_frequency_quartiles(
                self.view.user_train)
            text_index = fit_or_load_frozen_permitted_catalog_tfidf()
            plans = []
            for row in rows:
                t = last_nonpadding_physical_index(row.sequence)
                prefix = row.sequence[:t + 1]
                target = row.positive[t]
                repeat = target in nonpadding_ids(prefix)
                universe = text_index.nonzero_real_item_ids - set(prefix) - {target}
                matched = items_in_target_frequency_band(universe, target)
                neighbors = positive_cosine_neighbors(target, universe)
                reasons = eligibility_reasons(target, universe, matched,
                                              neighbors, required_size=32)
                record_individual_and_common_coverage(row, reasons)
                if reasons:
                    continue
                plans.append(freeze_plan(
                    row=row, target=target, universe=universe,
                    uniform=sample_unique(universe, 32, stable_row_stream(row, 0)),
                    frequency_matched=sample_unique(matched, 32, stable_row_stream(row, 1)),
                    text_neighbors=sort_similarity_then_item_id(neighbors)[:32],
                    repeat=repeat, frequency_band=band(target),
                    length_bin=fixed_length_bin(nonpadding_count(prefix))))
            for plan in plans:
                features = self.view.log2feats(plan.row.sequence.unsqueeze(0))
                t = last_nonpadding_physical_index(plan.row.sequence)
                feature = features[:, t:t + 1, :]
                # Adapter candidate shape: B x 1 x C; feature shape: B x 1 x D.
                model_top, universe_size = exact_chunked_topk(
                    self.view, feature, plan.universe, k=32,
                    ordering='score descending, item ID ascending')
                panels = plan.fixed_panels | {'model_high_score': model_top}
                record_panel_overlap_and_sizes(panels)
                for name, panel in panels.items():
                    scores = self.view.predict_score(
                        feature, tensor([plan.target] + panel).reshape(1, 1, 33))
                    if not all_finite(scores):
                        record_missing(name, reason='nonfinite scores')
                        continue
                    ahead = (scores[1:] > scores[0]) | (
                        (scores[1:] == scores[0]) & (panel_ids(panel) < plan.target))
                    record_paired_row(
                        plan, name, rank=1 + sum(ahead),
                        max_alternative_margin=scores[0] - max(scores[1:]),
                        outranking_fraction=mean(ahead),
                        score_ties=sum(scores[1:] == scores[0]),
                        universe_size=universe_size,
                        right_censored=(name == 'model_high_score' and sum(ahead) == 32))
            # Existing probes remain; empty measurements are null with reasons.
            return {
                'metrics': combine_existing_probes_with_descriptive_paired_summaries(
                    include_coverage=True, include_strata=True,
                    user_confidence_intervals=None),
                'metric_definitions': definitions_with_universe_ties_censoring_and_scope()
            }
    finally:
        self.view.model.train(was_training)

# Reproducibility checks: identity scoring agrees; top-K target rank equals
# min(exact declared-universe rank, 33), including an all-tied synthetic case;
# candidate IDs are unique and obey exclusions; text failures remain explicit.
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) embeds actual metrics/definitions
# and requests bounded hypotheses, never held-out-performance or preference claims.

originality.positive: Combines family-compatible scoring with common-cohort candidate controls, exact top-K interpretation and repeat-aware descriptive strata.
originality.negative: Candidate sampling, repeat stratification and rank censoring are established concepts; the contribution is careful integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish easy training-pair separation, candidate-selection effects and repeat-related advantages before committing budget to controlled HSTU training ablations.
future_potential.negative: Training-only diagnostics cannot establish generalization or current usefulness, and model-mined hardness adds no independent evidence beyond the underlying rank information.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses the existing HSTU and ModelView interfaces without additional trained predictors or checkpoint changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Shared eligibility, deterministic ties, metadata missingness, exact chunked retrieval, reproducible plans and dependence-aware summaries require more engineering than the original score of 3 suggested.

related_work.title: [1] Dallmann et al.: study of sampling strategies for recommendation evaluation
contributions: Investigates changes in recommendation model comparisons under sampled versus full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed four-panel diagnostic or predict improvement under the pinned RecHarness evaluator.

related_work.title: [2] Prakash et al. (2024): comparison of negative-sampling approaches in sequential recommendation
contributions: Examines sampling-dependent aggregate results and head, middle and tail item disparities.
limitations: Does not imply a universally optimal sampler or establish difficult unobserved items as confirmed negatives.

related_work.title: [3] ICLR 2024 study of activation-patching methodological choices
contributions: Shows that corruption and scoring choices influence activation-patching conclusions.
limitations: Application to the supplied HSTU requires architecture-specific intervention verification and cannot assume reference HSTU internals.

related_work.title: [4] TREC 2025 Product Recommendation track guidelines
contributions: Distinguishes functional substitutes, complements and unknown compatibility.
limitations: A relationship rubric cannot establish current need, ownership or compatibility when evidence is missing.

related_work.title: [5] Sufficient Context
contributions: Separates relevant information from sufficient evidence and studies guided abstention.
limitations: Recommendation-specific judgments require separate human calibration and coverage reporting.

related_work.title: [6] Krichene and Rendle (2020): On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes discrepancies between sampled ranking metrics and their full-catalog counterparts.
limitations: Does not make different candidate constructions interchangeable or justify replacing the pinned host evaluation.

related_work.title: [7] Exact model-top-K candidate rank identity: mathematical derivation supplied in reflection
contributions: Under exact retrieval over the same eligible universe and a consistent total order, the positive's panel rank is min(r,K+1).
Panel HR@h equals that universe's HR@h for h<=K; deeper ranks are right-censored.
limitations: This is a mathematical consequence, not an external empirical study.
Approximate retrieval, mismatched filtering or inconsistent ties invalidate the identity; a restricted universe does not establish full-catalog performance.

related_work.title: [8] RepeatNet: A Repeat Aware Neural Recommendation Machine for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Explicitly distinguishes repeat and explore recommendation behavior.
limitations: Does not establish repeat consumption as undesirable or require adopting its architecture; the proposed experiment preserves HSTU.

related_work.title: [9] Li et al., SIGIR 2023: repetition and shortcut behavior in recommendation
contributions: Examines repeat/explore difficulty differences and repetition-related shortcuts, including effects associated with shared embeddings.
limitations: Observed repeat advantages in this diagnostic would not alone prove memorization or establish the mechanism in the supplied HSTU.

related_work.title: [10] Cai et al. (2022): false negatives among recommendation candidates
contributions: Supports caution when treating highly ranked unobserved alternatives as irrelevant negatives.
limitations: Does not identify which alternatives are false negatives in this task.

related_work.title: [11] Candidate-set sampling and popularity effects
contributions: Motivates explicit candidate-construction and popularity controls.
limitations: The common-cohort four-panel design is a proposed adaptation, not a protocol established by this reference.

related_work.title: [12] Temporal leakage in recommendation evaluation
contributions: Motivates auditing whether diagnostic information was available at the relevant prediction time.
limitations: Historical metadata availability may be unverifiable here; the benchmark splits must remain unchanged.
